key_insight: PINN training can match full-space optimization within a small Hessian-eigenvector subspace selected by gradient alignment rather than curvature magnitude.
engineering_relevance: Gradient-aligned subspaces offer a foundation for optimizers tailored to the ill-conditioned loss landscapes of physics-informed PDE solvers.
method: Select the dominant aligned subspace (DAS) by gradient alignment, not eigenvalue magnitude.
Study DAS-restricted training with line search and extend the analysis to Gauss–Newton.
evidence_signal: Across Poisson, heat, wave, and viscous Burgers benchmarks, DAS-restricted training empirically matches full-space training even when the projected Hessian remains ill-conditioned.
watch_item: Full Hessian eigendecomposition is costly at scale, and the abstract does not establish end-to-end computational savings.
paper_title: A Systematic Analysis of a Small Optimal Subspace for Physics-Informed Neural Networks: $n$-DAS $\subset \mathbb{R}^p$
